observations: Single tyre shown from a top-down tread perspective.
A sticker on the tread identifies the tyre as a Bridgestone Alenza 001.
Sticker lists size as 275/50R20 109W and 'Made in Japan'.
Tread appears unused with visible factory color lines (red and blue).
The sidewall markings are not visible in the photo.
Watermark 'FRANCO GLOBAL ENTERPRISES' is visible across the image.

risks.risk: The manufacturing date (DOT code) is hidden; tyres degrade and become unsafe after 5-6 years regardless of tread.
risks.proof: A photo of the 4-digit DOT code embossed on the sidewall.

risks.risk: Sidewall damage, bulges, or internal repairs are not visible from the tread view.
risks.proof: Clear photos of both the inner and outer sidewalls.
risks.if_unproven: as having a structural defect or repair

risks.risk: The sticker may not match the actual tyre specifications embossed on the rubber.
risks.proof: A photo of the brand, model, and size embossed on the tyre sidewall.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic tyre of the same size

proof_requests: Photo of the 4-digit DOT code on the sidewall to confirm the year of manufacture.
Photos of both the inner and outer sidewalls to check for damage or repairs.
Photo of the brand and size markings embossed on the sidewall to verify the sticker's accuracy.
response.reason: The brand, model, and size are identified from the tread sticker. While the tyre appears new, it must be priced as old stock until the manufacturing date and sidewall integrity are confirmed.
